explanation: PolicyState is an enumeration, but the code kind Data class admits only 'A Class or Structure'. Policy data class and Working data class name enumerations explicitly, so the registry rules disagree with this choice. Re-assign by layer and say why, or justify Data class. The same holds for PolicyRegistryValueType (PolicyStructures.vb 22-26).

An enumeration is given Data class, whose rule names only a Class or Structure, while Policy data class lists enumerations. Re-assign or justify; see the challenge on PolicyState (PolicyProcessing.vb 426-431).

Data class admits a class 'holding only fields, with no members that run'. RegistryKeyValuePair also declares EqualsRKVP, Equals and GetHashCode (lines 436-445), each its own block. Choose a kind whose rule admits a data holder with equality members, or explain why the field part alone meets Data class.

PolEntryData is given Data class (no members that run) but lines 231-353 hold sixteen conversion methods, each its own block. Only its two fields (229-230) are the shape. Choose a kind that admits the field part of a class with methods, or justify Data class.
RegFileKey is given Data class (no members that run) yet declares GetValue (305-307), a block of its own. Say why the field part meets the kind, or use a kind that admits it.

Every shape in PolicyStructures.vb and PresentationStructures.vb is Data class, but the registry's Policy data class admits a plain class that only holds values read from policy (ADMX/ADML) files, with no screen controls. Two kinds admit the same lines. Decide the kind and layer, state why, and apply it to all definitions of these two files.

Field RegistryType is declared 'As PolicyRegistryValueType', an enumeration defined in this job (22-26), with no refersTo, while sibling fields typed with other shapes (OnValue, AffectedValues, Value, Items) have one. Add the reference.

Policy logic routine admits a method that decides a policy state, reads or writes a policy source, or enables a privilege. DeduplicatePolicies merges user and computer policies of an AdmxBundle workspace (117-129) and touches no policy source or state. Policy data routine admits methods that resolve policy definition data (AdmxBundle). The code leaves the kind open; decide and explain, or write the kind that fits.

IsPolicySupported decides whether a policy is supported on given products (382-423): not a policy state and not a policy source read or write, which is what Policy logic routine admits. It works on policy definition data. The code leaves the kind open; decide and explain, or write the kind that fits.

says: If one link per block and target is not the rule, SetPolicyState and GetPolicyOptionStates lose effects: SetPolicyState writes values on enable (SetValue 299-353), deletes on disable (DeleteValue 321, 358, 371, 374) and clears list keys (ClearKey 364), yet only SetValue at 273, DeleteValue at 271 and ClearKey at 330 are linked. GetPolicyState also calls WillDeleteValue at 52 and 63, GetPolicyOptionStates calls GetValue at 146/152/160/185 and GetValueNames at 164. Where a different call site decides a different effect, write that link at its own line; if the collapse is deliberate, keep it.

WalkPolicyRegistry line 218 (entries.Contains) runs RegistryKeyValuePair.Equals at run time, and the Equals and GetHashCode override blocks (439-445) are reached by no link. Add a call link to the Equals override (439-442) or say why not.
